source.title: Neural Network Training Techniques Regularize Optimization Trajectory: An Empirical Study
source.authors: Cheng Chen; Junjie Yang; Yi Zhou

record.tranche_reason: Compares training techniques and reports how they affect convergence in CIFAR training; the reported measure is training loss and convergence, not classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss curves and explicit comparisons of convergence speed. It does not report training classification error, zero error, or accuracy gains. Figure values are not recoverable from the supplied text. The activation-function and optimizer comparisons are not mapped to versions here.
record.test_reason: The study measures training-loss convergence and optimization-trajectory regularity. It does not measure V6's accuracy gains or learning-rate tolerance, V3's depth-dependent training-error degradation, or the outcomes and interventions named by the other versions. Its related optimization results therefore fit no supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors propose a trajectory regularity principle, prove a conditional convergence bound, and report that faster-converging training configurations generally have larger regularity parameters. They interpret this association as training techniques regularizing update directions to facilitate convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study empirically compares training techniques using optimization-trajectory regularity and training loss; it does not reproduce the claim's training-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Convergence descriptions vary with activation function, batch-normalization configuration, skip-connection count, optimizer, network, and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing all BN layers substantially slows training-loss convergence. Keeping the first BN layer per block is as fast as keeping all layers in the described CIFAR-10 VGG experiments; keeping all is slightly faster on CIFAR-100. Similar ResNet observations are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization accelerates training-loss convergence in the tested VGG and ResNet configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Keeping more skip connections accelerates training-loss convergence in the tested ResNets and U-Net. This does not establish depth-dependent classification-error degradation or its prevention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retaining more skip connections accelerates training-loss convergence in these configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation comparisons favor ReLU variants in the classification experiments and sigmoid in U-Net regression; initialization methods are not compared.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The activation function associated with faster training-loss convergence depends on the tested architecture and task.

fits_no_version.finding: Faster loss convergence is associated with larger trajectory-regularity parameters; Adam converges fastest in the reported optimizer comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trajectory regularity characterizes convergence differences among the tested training techniques and optimizers.

record.peer_reviewed: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (Big Data)
record.problems: Results are primarily plotted; the supplied text gives qualitative convergence descriptions but no extractable numerical training-loss values or uncertainty estimates. Training classification error is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the reported outcome is training loss/convergence, while the claim versions specify classification error or accuracy gains. Figure-only values cannot supply those outcomes.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training classification-error degradation in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, initialization-dependent training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases and recovery, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Faster accuracy gains with batch normalization, tolerance of higher learning rates, and Fixup comparisons. Training-loss convergence is reported, but accuracy and learning-rate tolerance are not.

record.verdict_notes: Change V6 from tested_not_extracted to not tested under the supplied outcome-specific wording. There are no extracted rows to fix. The loss-curve results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model size are not reported.
No teacher-student problem or neuron-width sweep.
The paper varies skip connections but does not report classification error or compare plain and residual networks on the claimed depth-related training-error outcome.
Activation functions are compared, but initialization methods, signal propagation, and trainable depth are not tested.
No learning-rate stability threshold, curvature, or loss-recovery experiment.

Batch normalization conditions and convergence speed are described, but the study reports training-loss curves rather than accuracy or classification error, so no row directly measures the version's stated accuracy-gain outcome.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
